clue.text: Pit foreign articles against vast number

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article and DER a German definite article
a world of things is a huge amount of them

explanation.surface: A miner compares overseas newspaper features with an enormous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' reads like newspaper pieces, but means grammatical articles: French UN and German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The pit is the infernal region below, the land of the dead in myth.

clue.text: Variable rate of progress cutting music company's work

indicators.note: cutting says the speed letters slice into the company name

parts.note: Sony is a large music and electronics company
Y is a standard algebraic symbol for an unknown variable
mph, miles per hour, measures speed of travel

explanation.surface: A record label's output is cut into by some fluctuating speed of advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' looks like an adjective qualifying the rate, but it is a lone algebra letter in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is an orchestral composition, an example of a musical work.

clue.text: Pretty smart penning melody

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the tune sits inside the word for smart

parts.note: fly is informal British for sharp-witted or knowing
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Someone well dressed is writing a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' is the adverb, as in pretty good, not the adjective for good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning moderately or to some degree, as in quite good.

clue.text: Catch woman's aria finally coming in

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the final letter goes inside the possessive word

parts.note: her is the possessive belonging to a woman

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word aria

explanation.surface: An opera-goer catches the singer's aria as it reaches its last notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts A, the last letter of aria, inside HER.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch what someone says is to make it out with your ears.

clue.text: Carmen's pet distressed Cliff

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Carmen's beloved animal upset a man called Cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' poses as a man's name; it is the definition, a steep rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope or rock face, a kind of cliff.

clue.text: One of his works lied

parts.note: a lied is a German art song, and this Austrian composer wrote hundreds of them

explanation.surface: An accusation that some creator was dishonest in one of his productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' reads as the past of lie, but it is the German noun for a song; the composer is the one whose works include lieder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer of Erlkönig and Winterreise is the master of German song.

clue.text: Make mistake with delivery perhaps

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and means together with

explanation.surface: A courier slips up on a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a parcel somewhere is a typical short trip on someone's behalf, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Regret bringing in Latin canon

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so the abbreviation goes within the word for regret

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Remorse at introducing Latin into church law.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a law or principle, especially a church one.

clue.text: They oppose any crazy crime writer

indicators.note: crazy says the three letters of any are scrambled

parts.note: Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.surface: Critics object to some mad mystery novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles ANY into NAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual objectors are people who always say no to proposals.

clue.text: Horn, gold with new copper coating

indicators.note: coating means covering the outside, so the copper symbol wraps the other letters

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A musical horn made of gold with a fresh copper plating.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornu is the Latin anatomical term for a horn-shaped structure, and also an ancient Roman brass instrument.

clue.text: Theatre in his city backed Nero for one

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the assembled letters run in reverse
in says the theatre word goes inside the city name

parts.note: Nero's city is Rome, where he ruled
rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre in Nero's home city supported him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like supported, but it reverses everything before it; 'his' refers forward to Nero, which with 'for one' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman ruler, an example of a monarch over an empire.

clue.text: Notice Unionist who's left us flatter

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
the late person is one who has died, departed from us

explanation.surface: A political obituary notice for a Unionist, which is less than honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like a comparative of flat but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter is to praise excessively; adulation is fawning admiration.

clue.text: Part-time clarinettist loves to go in with dry lips

indicators.note: to go in means the two O's are placed inside the other letters
the lips of a word are its outer letters, here those of dry

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so loves are two O's

explanation.surface: A weekend reed-player likes to start a session with parched lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loves' looks like a verb but is two tennis zeros; W for with is a common crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Allen, the film director, also plays clarinet with a jazz band in his spare time.

clue.text: Mozart's first work made for Shaggy?

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Mozart's

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to make for a place is to head towards it, so made for means headed

explanation.surface: Mozart's debut composition was written for someone called Shaggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaggy' poses as a name; the question mark flags it as a description of unruly hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a thick untidy mass of hair could be described as shaggy.

clue.text: Flutes flop, then son's hurled missiles

parts.note: to mill is to cut grooves or ridges, as on a coin edge, which is to flute it
a bomb is a failure, a flop
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A wind section's poor show, after which a boy throws things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutes' reads as the instruments but is a verb meaning grooves.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mills bomb was a British hand grenade of the First World War, a thrown explosive.

clue.text: Having bizarre ideas, fried andouilles

indicators.note: fried suggests something cooked and broken up, so the letters of the sausages are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eating fried French tripe sausages starts having strange thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: Andouilles are French sausages made from pork intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: A person holding false beliefs out of touch with reality has fantastical notions.

clue.text: Three men and a woman left large auditorium

parts.note: the three men are Roy, Al and Al
Bertha is a woman's name
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Three men and a woman walked out of a large concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb, departed, but is L; 'large' is a second L, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed Kensington concert venue, home of the Proms, is London's most famous performance space.

clue.text: Don't move doctor I googled

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A patient told to stay still after confessing to searching symptoms online.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is an idiom meaning keep still and hidden, like a dog playing dead.

clue.text: Nearly all old characters produce wind

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the thorn is an Old English letter, so thorns are old characters

explanation.surface: Almost every elderly person gives off gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops a letter from ALL. 'characters' are letters here, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto horns are brass instruments, and brass instruments belong to the wind family.

clue.text: Service originally designed by clique?

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of designed

parts.note: an inner set is a select exclusive group

explanation.surface: A church service first devised by an exclusive circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks religious but is a set of tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a full matching set of plates and dishes for meals.

clue.text: Plant food court close to boxes

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the word for close holds the court letters

parts.note: near means close to

explanation.surface: A food court next to some packaging units sells vegetable fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant food' looks like fertiliser; it is the sugary liquid flowers produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers secrete this sweet fluid, which bees and butterflies feed on.

clue.text: They come into a cathedral to sing

indicators.note: things that come into words are found inside them, so the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: Visitors arrive at a cathedral to join in the singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of choristers, but only 'They' defines; the rest hides the answer across 'cathedral to sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to choir singers of the voice part just above tenor, the people the surface describes.

clue.text: Like Schoenberg, obsessive about limits of tempo

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for obsessive goes round the two letters

parts.note: anal is informal for fussy and obsessive

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters, here those of tempo

explanation.surface: A composer is fussy about keeping strict time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is the container signal, with the obsessive word wrapped round the tempo letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoenberg wrote music without a key, abandoning tonality.

clue.text: High wind still cool everywhere

parts.note: a still is a photograph, a pic

indicators.note: everywhere suggests letters scattered about, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strong breeze is still chilly all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High wind' reads as a gale; it is a high-pitched wind instrument. 'everywhere' scrambles COOL into COLO.
explanation.definitionFit: The piccolo is the small flute that plays highest in the orchestra's woodwind.

clue.text: Run out during afternoon dance in US school

indicators.note: during means within the time span, so the cricket letters go inside the afternoon letters

parts.note: pm stands for post meridiem, the afternoon
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A student flees in the middle of an afternoon school dance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter can be dismissed 'run out', recorded as RO on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom is the formal dance held at an American high school.

clue.text: Tender part of basso so romantic in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bass singer delivers a gentle passage in a very romantic way, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Tender part' as the definition, leaving the hidden word with no indicator; 'part of' signals the hiding, so the definition is just 'Tender'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso is the musical direction meaning lovingly, to be played with tenderness.

clue.text: Eager to help, introducing Verdi overture

indicators.note: introducing means putting in, so the opening letter goes inside the word for help

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: an overture is an opening, so it takes the first letter of Verdi

explanation.surface: Keen to assist by playing the opening of a Verdi opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keenly enthusiastic, as in an avid reader.

clue.text: Primate called after Beethoven's Sixth

indicators.note: after says the word for called comes behind the picked letter
Sixth picks the sixth letter of Beethoven's

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: An ape is named after Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sixth' reads as the symphony but means the sixth letter of Beethoven: O.
explanation.definitionFit: The orangutan, often shortened, is a great ape and so a primate.

clue.text: Brian and I arranged to import brown sort of metal

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the colour goes inside the rearranged letters
arranged means set out in order, so the letters of Brian and I are reordered

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Two musicians arranged a piece to bring in a brown sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link here: the letters of Brian and I alone are rearranged, with the colour set inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia metal is a pewter-like alloy of tin, antimony and copper.
